mine: No one born of a forbidden union
note: Hebrew mamzer (only here and Zech 9:6) is of uncertain meaning; Jewish tradition takes it as the offspring of incest or adultery, not simply a child born out of wedlock as "bastard" implies. (Hebrew 23:3 = KJV 23:2.) Context: one born of a forbidden union (medium confidence). Mamzer occurs only here and Zech 9:6. Rabbinic law (m. Yevamot 4:13) takes it as the child of incest or adultery; the LXX has 'son of a harlot'. 'Forbidden union' (ESV; NIV, NRSV similar) covers these without the English sense of any child born out of wedlock. The precise reference stays uncertain. Other possible meanings: (1) 'child of a prostitute' — LXX ek pornes, Vulgate de scorto natus; (2) 'bastard', a child born outside marriage — KJV, NASB 'of illegitimate birth'; (3) a person of mixed or foreign descent — some commentators from Zech 9:6 and the following ban on Ammonites and Moabites; NJPS 'misbegotten' leaves it open.
